title: Surface Area Calculator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: High School Geometry
description: Choose a prism, cube, cylinder, pyramid, cone, or sphere, set its dimensions, and follow the surface area calculation step by step.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to calculate the surface area of prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres and analyze how changing a dimension affects the surface area.
prerequisites: Parts of solids: base, lateral face, slant height

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked examples with the solution steps that can be hidden for self-checking
keyQuestions: Which term of the cylinder formula is the curved side?
Why does a cone's formula use the slant height and not the vertical height?
How does the surface area change when every dimension doubles?
commonMisconceptions: Slant height and vertical height are the same.
Surface area and volume grow at the same rate.
A cylinder's surface area is just 2πrh (that omits the two circular bases).
assessmentOpportunities: Students compute the surface area of a cone with radius 6 and slant height 10 by hand, then decide whether a cone with radius 6 and slant height 5 can exist and justify the answer.
